facts.label: GDP per person in 1970
facts.detail: In current US dollars, Sweden was about 44% richer per person than Norway.

facts.label: GDP per person in 2024

facts.label: Norway's geologists on offshore oil
facts.detail: The Geological Survey of Norway wrote to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs that finding coal, oil or sulphur on the continental shelf could be discounted.
facts.videoTitle: Why Is Norway Richer Than Sweden?

facts.label: North Sea split by the median line
facts.detail: Agreements with the United Kingdom (March) and Denmark (December) divided the continental shelf along the median line.
facts.videoTitle: Why Is Norway Richer Than Sweden?

facts.label: Ekofisk discovered
facts.detail: Phillips Petroleum reported it just before Christmas. One of the largest offshore oil fields ever discovered; production began on 15 June 1971.
facts.videoTitle: Why Is Norway Richer Than Sweden?

facts.label: Marginal tax rate on oil profits
facts.detail: The ordinary 22% company tax plus a special petroleum tax.
facts.videoTitle: Why Is Norway Richer Than Sweden?

facts.label: Norway's oil fund (30 September 2026)
facts.detail: About $2.3 trillion. The fund invests only abroad, so the Norwegian economy does not overheat.
facts.videoTitle: Why Is Norway Richer Than Sweden?

facts.label: Former name
facts.detail: Until 1945 the city was German, part of East Prussia.
facts.videoTitle: Kaliningrad: Why Does Russia Own It?

facts.label: Transferred to the USSR
facts.detail: The Potsdam Agreement of August 1, 1945 placed Königsberg and the northern part of East Prussia under the Soviet Union.
facts.videoTitle: Kaliningrad: Why Does Russia Own It?

facts.label: Renamed Kaliningrad
facts.detail: The city was renamed after Mikhail Kalinin.
facts.videoTitle: Kaliningrad: Why Does Russia Own It?

facts.label: Cut off from mainland Russia
facts.detail: The USSR recognised Lithuania's independence on September 6, 1991, and the Soviet Union itself dissolved in December 1991.
facts.videoTitle: Kaliningrad: Why Does Russia Own It?

facts.label: Neighbours in NATO and the EU
facts.detail: Poland joined NATO in 1999 and Lithuania on March 29, 2004; both joined the EU on May 1, 2004.
facts.videoTitle: Kaliningrad: Why Does Russia Own It?

facts.label: Ice-free port
facts.detail: Home of Russia's Baltic Fleet and Russia's only Baltic port that stays free of ice all year.
facts.videoTitle: Kaliningrad: Why Does Russia Own It?

facts.label: Area and population
facts.detail: A small exclave compared with the rest of Russia.
facts.videoTitle: Kaliningrad: Why Does Russia Own It?

facts.label: Purchase price
facts.detail: The sum the United States agreed to pay Russia for Alaska in 1867.
facts.videoTitle: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre

facts.label: Treaty signed
facts.detail: Signed in Washington by US Secretary of State William Seward and Russian minister Eduard de Stoeckl, at 4 a.m. after negotiating through the night.
facts.videoTitle: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre

facts.label: Senate vote
facts.detail: The US Senate ratified the treaty on April 9, 1867.
facts.videoTitle: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre

facts.label: Formal handover
facts.detail: In Sitka, the Russian flag was lowered and the US flag was raised.
facts.videoTitle: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre

facts.label: Price per acre
facts.detail: Roughly 1,518,800 km² (375 million acres) for $7.2 million works out to about 1.9 cents an acre.
facts.videoTitle: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre

facts.label: Size compared with France
facts.detail: Alaska has about 1,481,346 km² of land, against about 543,940 km² for metropolitan France.
facts.videoTitle: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre

facts.label: Prudhoe Bay oil discovery
facts.detail: Prudhoe Bay is the largest oil field in the United States.
facts.videoTitle: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre

facts.label: Alaska oil output in 2026
facts.detail: At around $100 a barrel, that is roughly $7 million worth of oil every four hours.
